visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A young boy with short black hair stands on a grey padded mat in a modern indoor living room. He is dressed in a navy blue polo shirt featuring a white '3' on the sleeve and khaki shorts, holding a black pen in his right hand. The background shows a light-colored wooden table with a water bottle and a wooden slatted door. (2) The boy looks down at the mat and begins to stomp his feet rhythmically, swinging his arms in a repetitive motion. A red exclamation mark graphic appears above his head briefly as he starts his coordinated movements. (3) He continues the rhythmic stomping and arm-swinging, looking intensely focused. Dynamic purple text graphics reading 'Rock you!!' appear and disappear around him as he moves. (4) The boy stops his rhythmic movement and stands still, looking off-camera with a neutral expression. A red and white subtitle appears at the bottom of the frame over the mat as the camera remains focused on him in a medium shot.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The audio begins with a series of rhythmic thuds, appearing to be footsteps or stomping against a resonant surface. A female adult voice then enters, singing 'We will, we will' with a moderate pitch and high enthusiasm, mimicking a well-known rock anthem's cadence. (2) The rhythmic thumping continues as a structured beat. The female voice then shouts 'Rock you!' with significantly increased loudness and intensity, exhibiting a sharp pitch contour and high arousal. (3) The pattern of thumps followed by the shouted phrase 'Rock you!' repeats several times. The female voice maintains an excited, slightly comedic tone. (4) The rhythmic thumping stops. The female voice transitions from singing to speaking, saying '你可以先學會兒歌嗎' (Can you learn children's songs first?) in a friendly, teasing tone followed by the sound of light laughter.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video humorousy depicts a young child mimicking the rhythmic stomping and vocal cues of Queen's 'We Will Rock You' as a result of his mother playing and singing it frequently to relieve parenting stress. It captures a cute and funny domestic moment where the toddler's imitation of 'rock' energy contrasts with his mother's lighthearted suggestion that he should learn nursery rhymes instead.

high_inference.freeDescribe: The child's coordination with the off-camera audio cues is the primary comedic element.
